text:
Sofia Ivanova: seeing a perf regression after enabling quant profiles (int8) on long-context traffic. p95 for 16k+ prompts went from ~1.9s -> ~3.4s on A100 pool (hosted). short ctx looks fine. anyone else seeing this?

perfbot: Alert: route=chat/longctx p95_latency_ms +78% (baseline window 30m) tag exec_mode=quantized profile=qpl:qwen2.5-72b:int8:v1.2.0 gpu=a100

Mateo Alvarez: :eyes: do we know if it’s all longctx routes or specifically the 16k+ bin? also which model + profile?

Sofia Ivanova: mostly 16k-32k seq len bin. model is `qwen2.5-72b` (hosted) with `int8` profile (v1.2.0). p50 is only slightly up, but tail is ugly.

Hiro Tanaka: could be kernel path change for long seq. int8 path might be falling off flash-attn v2 and using something slower (esp if we lose paged kv optimizations). do we have kernel tags from traces?

Logan Wright: we do (from PR 28833). quick look in honeycomb: quantized requests in longctx are hitting `attn_kernel=sdpa_ref` more often than baseline (`flash_v2`). that would explain tail.

Mateo Alvarez: ok that’s promising. Sofia can you paste a couple trace snippets / runtime logs? want to confirm it’s not a fallback loop.

Sofia Ivanova: pulled from one worker (redacted). notice it says “flash disabled due to dtype/layout mismatch”:
```log
2024-11-07T19:12:04.991Z runtime INFO req_id=01JCBJ... model=qwen2.5-72b seq_in=17842 seq_out=512 gpu=a100-sm80
2024-11-07T19:12:04.991Z runtime INFO qpl_profile_id=qpl:qwen2.5-72b:int8 qpl_version=1.2.0 exec_mode=quantized
2024-11-07T19:12:04.992Z kernels WARN flash_attn_v2 disabled: unsupported qkv_layout=packed_int8 for head_dim=128 (expected fp16/bf16)
2024-11-07T19:12:04.992Z kernels INFO selecting attn=sdpa_ref reason=flash_disabled
2024-11-07T19:12:08.233Z runtime INFO finished req_id=01JCBJ... t_total_ms=3241 t_prefill_ms=2894 t_decode_ms=347
```

Hiro Tanaka: yep. for int8 we’re packing QKV and that path doesn’t have flash kernel coverage for head_dim=128 (or at least not wired). baseline stays fp16/bf16 -> flash.

Yuki Sato: this might be related to the “packed_int8” change we merged for that profile family. we assumed longctx perf would still be fine due to smaller memory footprint, but if we lose flash it’s a net loss.

Marcus Reed: corroborating from perf suite history: last night’s A100 run for qwen2.5-72b int8 looked ok at 4k/8k but we didn’t run 16k+ with realistic batch shapes (my bad). our current suite bins stop at 8192 for that job.

Jonas Weber: from eval/perf side: we only signed off quality for 16k prompts, but perf gate was “>=10% cheaper tokens/$ on 8k synthetic”. no longctx latency guardrail.

Mateo Alvarez: ok, so likely: quant profile is “valid” but runtime kernel selection makes it slower for long seq. we need an immediate mitigation + longer-term kernel fix.

Rafael Mendes: what’s the blast radius? is this on a canary toggle or fully enabled?

Sofia Ivanova: canary 25% on `chat/longctx` org default. but traffic skew means a lot of 16k+ gets routed through that route, so users notice.

Rafael Mendes: recommend we drop canary to 0% for that route while we investigate. also we should add an auto-disable condition tied to `seq_in` bins, but that’s not in the policy engine yet.

Mateo Alvarez: agree. Sofia can you disable quant on `chat/longctx` now? (route-level toggle)

Sofia Ivanova: on it. setting `quantization.enabled=false` for that route. will keep it enabled for other routes.

Nadia Rahman: heads up: cost attribution shows quant path is cheaper per token, but if latency explodes we may reduce throughput / increase retries. on this route, we’re also seeing `client_cancel_rate` up.

Logan Wright: query results:
- baseline: `attn_kernel=flash_v2` ~92% of requests in seq_in>16k
- quantized: `attn_kernel=sdpa_ref` ~88% in seq_in>16k
also `kv_cache_evictions` up 3x on quantized in that bin (maybe because prefill slower => queueing => cache pressure)

Hiro Tanaka: the “unsupported qkv_layout=packed_int8” is pretty definitive. we can do one of:
1) update compat check: if seq_in >= X (or if model head_dim=128 + packed_int8), force baseline dtype to keep flash
2) add a new int8 kernel path for flash (bigger lift)
3) split profile into 2 variants: int8 for <=8k, fp16/bf16 for longctx

Mateo Alvarez: immediate: (1) in runtime selection, add a guard to not pick that profile for longctx requests if it will disable flash. that keeps QPL opt-in but avoids perf cliffs.

Yuki Sato: where to implement? in profile resolver we have access to `seq_len_regime` already (short/medium/long). we can add `constraints.sequence_length_max` to profile manifest and have resolver reject.

Mateo Alvarez: yep. if we can’t change profile manifest fast, we can hardcode a temporary runtime denylist keyed by `profile_id + seq_in>=8192`.

Sofia Ivanova: route toggle change applied. initial metrics look better already (p95 dropping).

perfbot: Recovery: route=chat/longctx p95_latency_ms back within 10% of baseline (exec_mode=baseline dominant)

Marcus Reed: for follow-up: I can extend perf suite bins to 16k/32k with load shapes matching longctx route (prefill-heavy). will take a day to wire in benchmark-lab.

Jonas Weber: +1. also we should add perf acceptance threshold language: “do not ship profile if disables flash for seq_len>8k unless explicitly scoped.”

Hiro Tanaka: can I get GPU SKU detail? is this only A100 or also H100/L40S?

Sofia Ivanova: saw it on A100 (sm80) primarily. didn’t check H100 yet (sm90). logs all show same `packed_int8` layout though.

Hiro Tanaka: on H100 we might have different kernels available, but our code still selects based on layout. likely same issue unless we special-case.

Mateo Alvarez: action items:
- [runtime] add compat guard: if profile results in `attn_kernel != flash_v2` AND seq_in>8192 => fallback baseline (or reject profile). Hiro/Yuki can you take?
- [perf] Marcus extend suite for 16k/32k bins
- [telemetry] Logan add a quick dashboard slice: `attn_kernel` by seq bin and exec_mode
- [policy] Rafael: confirm route toggle is enough for customer comms; consider interim guidance (don’t enable quant on longctx routes)

Rafael Mendes: for comms: I’ll post in #incidents-lite + support note. also, do we need a postmortem? this is customer-visible.

Mateo Alvarez: probably a short retro. not a sev1 since we had canary, but still a miss.

Sofia Ivanova: one more datapoint: when quant was enabled, scheduler queue depth spiked, so even baseline requests on same pool got some tail impact. once disabled, queue recovered.

Logan Wright: adding snippet from trace tags for one of the bad ones:
```json
{"req_id":"01JCBJ...","route":"chat/longctx","model":"qwen2.5-72b","seq_in":17842,"exec_mode":"quantized","qpl_id":"qpl:qwen2.5-72b:int8","qpl_version":"1.2.0","attn_kernel":"sdpa_ref","prefill_ms":2894,"decode_ms":347,"gpu":"a100-sm80"}
```

Hiro Tanaka: I’ll open a runtime PR today with the guard + extra log line explaining why profile was rejected (so users aren’t confused by “enabled but not applied”).

Mateo Alvarez: make sure the rejection increments a counter + includes `reason=longctx_flash_incompatible` so we can track.

Yuki Sato: also suggest we update the qpl manifest for this profile: add `sequence_length_max: 8192` and `notes: longctx falls back due to flash incompatibility`.

Jonas Weber: +1, but please do runtime guard first (faster). I can coordinate manifest change with Arjun / profile owners.

Sofia Ivanova: thanks all. I’ll keep monitoring. if p95 drifts again I’ll ping.

Mateo Alvarez: appreciate the quick catch. let’s treat this as a gating requirement before expanding int8 to other longctx models.
